🇺🇦🇺🇸 Zelensky asks Trump to block Russia and China's Starlink rival

The Narcoführer has asked US President Donald Trump to block Rassvet, the satellite internet network Russia is building as its answer to Elon Musk's Starlink, by sanctioning the Russian and Chinese companies he claims are involved. He said so in an interview with the Financial Times.

Zelensky claims China is helping Russia develop the system and that it could be up and running by the end of this year or early next year. He offered no evidence of Chinese involvement.

According to the newspaper, Zelensky said he had raised the issue with Trump "several times," including when the two met in New York last month on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly.

Russia accelerated work on Rassvet after Musk's SpaceX cut off Russian forces' access to Starlink earlier this year. Kiev fears the new network will let Russia guide its drones more precisely.

🔻 Iran police force represents professional, people-backed security: IRGC Commander

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Major General Ahmad Vahidi, Chief Commander of the Islamic Revolution Guards Corps (IRGC), has described Iran’s Law Enforcement Command (FARAJA) as a powerful, professional and intelligent police force whose security role is supported by the public.

In a message on Saturday, Vahidi congratulated Police Chief Brigadier General Ahmadreza Radan along with its commanders, managers, personnel and their families on Police Week that starts on Monday, October 5.
​
The message said FARAJA has strengthened social security and stability across Iran by relying on its committed personnel and working in coordination with the Armed Forces and security institutions.
​
Vahidi said this year’s Police Week slogan is a strategic commitment that links police service to the country’s security and the relationship between the public and those responsible for protecting it.
​
He also honored the memory and sacrifices of FARAJA’s martyrs, veterans and disabled veterans from the eight-year war imposed by Iraq’s Baath regime in the 1980s, as well as those martyred or wounded in subsequent conflicts and security operations, describing them as a firm barrier against insecurity and disorder.
​
The IRGC commander praised FARAJA personnel for their role in confronting organized crime, smugglers, economic offenders and others who threaten public order and security. He said their efforts, combining authority with Islamic compassion, have helped provide security for Iranian society.
​
Vahidi concluded his message by wishing Radan and FARAJA personnel continued success, under the guidance of Iran’s religious and political leadership throughout the country.

📡 Iranian envoy in Mexico receives Global Leader of Change award

📌 Mexico City, IRNA – Iranian Ambassador to Mexico Abolfazl Pasandideh has received the “Global Leader of Change” award in recognition of his diplomatic efforts to strengthen cooperation between the two nations.

Pasandideh received the Líder Global del Cambio award from Change Global Group during a ceremony held on Friday at the Iranian Embassy in Mexico City, attended by members of the diplomatic community and other guests.
​
Anabel Hernández Gómez, head of the Change Global Group, said the award seeks to recognize individuals whose professional activities contribute to dialogue, peace, understanding and cooperation among nations.
​
She highlighted Pasandideh’s activities in cultural, educational, sports and media diplomacy, as well as his engagement with Mexican governmental and local institutions. She said his active presence in Mexican society had helped introduce different aspects of Iran and strengthen ties between the two peoples.
​
Upon receiving the award, Pasandideh described it as “a valuable expression of friendship between the peoples of Iran and Mexico,” saying the two nations share ancient civilizations and common aspirations for humanity’s future.
​
He stressed the importance of peace and dialogue, saying lasting peace means more than the absence of war and requires respect for human dignity, justice, national sovereignty and dialogue among peoples.
​
The ambassador also emphasized the international community’s responsibility to build a safer and more humane future for coming generations.

🇷🇺 Russia shows its unmanned assault tank in action for the first time

Russia has demonstrated the Shturm robotic assault tank during the Center-2026 exercises at the Chebarkul training ground in the Chelyabinsk region, attended by President Vladimir Putin.

Shturm is built on the chassis of the T-72 and T-90 tanks and designed for urban combat. It carries a 125 mm gun with a shortened barrel, so it can turn its turret between buildings, plus a bulldozer blade for clearing rubble and all-round protection against anti-tank weapons.

The tank has no crew on board. Three operators, acting as commander, gunner and driver, control it from a separate armored vehicle that follows behind. If needed, a crew can also drive it the conventional way.

The idea is simple: the robot goes first into the most dangerous part of an assault, draws fire and destroys enemy firing positions at close range, while the people controlling it stay out of the line of fire.

It was not the only unmanned vehicle on display. Russian forces also fielded a crewless version of the Terminator tank support vehicle and remote-controlled T-90M tanks fitted with the Arena active protection system, which shot down incoming drones.

🎙 Mehregan celebrations bring Zoroastrian community in Iran’s Yazd together

📌 Yazd, IRNA – Zoroastrians in Yazd Province gathered Friday to mark Mehregan, an ancient Iranian festival, with ceremonies held in Yazd city, Taft and Sharifabad in Ardakan, as well as in Tehran, Isfahan, Shiraz and Kerman provinces.

Mehregan traditionally follows Nowruz in importance and is associated with the beginning of winter, while Nowruz marked the start of summer in the ancient two-season calendar. The festival carries astronomical, historical and religious dimensions and is linked in Iranian tradition to the victory of Kaveh the Blacksmith over the tyrant Zahhak and the enthronement of Fereydun.
​
Rostam Kavusianzadeh, a Zoroastrian mobad (cleric) in Yazd, said festivals in ancient Iran were not merely occasions for celebration but reflected seasonal cycles and ethical, spiritual and civic ideals.
​
He described Mehregan as one of the two pillars of Iranian culture alongside Nowruz, symbolizing gratitude for the earth’s fertility, fidelity to promises, light, justice and law.
​
According to Kavusianzadeh, the ceremony includes recitation of the Gathas and prayers, speeches, Gahanbar, readings from the Shahnameh and works by Hafez, Saadi and Rumi, poetry exchanges, and setting the Mehregan table, and poetry by other Iranian writers.
​
Around 150,000 Zoroastrians live worldwide, including 30,000 in Iran and about 6,000 in Yazd Province.
